# @moku-labs/system

> Isomorphic system API for Moku apps — store, tray, notify, clipboard, and deep-link
> capabilities behind an env-style provider seam. A Tauri provider is selected when the
> native shell is detected; a web provider is the fallback. The same island code runs
> unchanged on web and native. Built on @moku-labs/core (micro-kernel) and
> @moku-labs/common (logPlugin -> ctx.log, envPlugin -> ctx.env).

Package: @moku-labs/system 0.1.0 (ESM + CJS, types included, sideEffects: false)
Repo: https://github.com/moku-labs/system
Full reference: llms-full.txt

## Core concepts

### 1. The provider seam (ctx.runtime)

- A core plugin named `runtime` is auto-registered (alongside logPlugin + envPlugin).
  It detects the shell ONCE at createApp:
  - kind: "tauri" when the Tauri 2 marker (__TAURI_INTERNALS__) is on globalThis, else "web"
  - platform: "macos" | "windows" | "linux" | "ios" | "android" | "unknown" (UA heuristics;
    "unknown" is the honest fallback, including SSR)
- The result is injected as `ctx.runtime` ({ kind, platform }) on every plugin context.
- Each capability plugin resolves its provider from that detection at app.start(),
  fire-and-forget: resolution failures fold into the NEXT method call's result, never
  into a startup throw.
- Overridable for tests via pluginConfigs: { runtime: { forceKind, forcePlatform } }.
- Island/consumer code must NEVER branch on the runtime itself — the plugin does.

### 2. The SystemResult contract (typed outcomes, never throws)

Every capability method returns SystemResult<T>:

    type SystemOk<T>  = { ok: true; value: T; provider: "tauri" | "web" };
    type SystemErr    = { ok: false; provider: "tauri" | "web";
                          reason: "unsupported" | "denied" | "unavailable" | "error";
                          message?: string };
    type SystemResult<T> = SystemOk<T> | SystemErr;

Reason semantics:
- unsupported  — capability permanently absent here (tray on web; tray on Tauri
                 iOS/Android; clipboard in insecure contexts). Hide the feature.
- denied       — unambiguous permission refusal (notify permission not granted;
                 clipboard NotAllowedError). Thrown errors are NEVER mapped to denied.
- unavailable  — environment cannot deliver right now (provider failed to resolve,
                 app not started, Safari private-mode storage probe failed).
- error        — provider threw during the operation; raw message preserved.

Environmental failure is data. Programmer errors (e.g. empty store.name) still throw
normally — fail-fast TypeError at createApp (onInit).

### 3. Subpath exports (zero-leak bundles)

Plugin INSTANCES are imported from subpaths, never the root:

    import { createApp, createPlugin, ok, err } from "@moku-labs/system"; // + types only
    import { storePlugin }     from "@moku-labs/system/store";
    import { trayPlugin }      from "@moku-labs/system/tray";
    import { notifyPlugin }    from "@moku-labs/system/notify";
    import { clipboardPlugin } from "@moku-labs/system/clipboard";
    import { deepLinkPlugin }  from "@moku-labs/system/deep-link";

Why: a root barrel re-exporting instances leaked ~2 KB gz of unimported capability code
into every consumer (measured). With subpaths, a store-only app carries zero bytes of
tray/notify/clipboard/deep-link. Root also re-exports type namespaces: Store, Tray,
Notify, Clipboard, DeepLink, plus SystemResult / SystemOk / SystemErr /
SystemErrorReason / RuntimeKind / RuntimePlatform / JsonValue / JsonPrimitive.

### 4. Optional Tauri peers

@tauri-apps/api, @tauri-apps/plugin-store, @tauri-apps/plugin-notification,
@tauri-apps/plugin-clipboard-manager, @tauri-apps/plugin-deep-link are OPTIONAL peer
dependencies — dynamically imported only inside Tauri providers when the native shell
is detected. Pure-web consumers do not install them.

## Quick reference

### Create and start an app

    import { createApp } from "@moku-labs/system";
    import { storePlugin } from "@moku-labs/system/store";

    const system = createApp({
      plugins: [storePlugin],
      pluginConfigs: { store: { name: "my-app" } }
    });
    await system.start();          // provider resolution kicks off here
    // ... use system.<capability>.<method>()
    await system.stop();           // disposes providers

Calling a method before start() resolves to
{ ok: false, reason: "unavailable", message: "app not started — call app.start() first" }.

### Per-capability one-liners

    // store — JSON-safe key-value persistence
    const r = await system.store.get<number>("count");    // SystemResult<number | undefined>
    await system.store.set("count", 1);                   // durable when ok
    await system.store.delete("count");
    await system.store.keys();                            // SystemResult<string[]>
    await system.store.clear();

    // tray — desktop only; web + Tauri mobile answer err("unsupported")
    await system.tray.setMenu([{ id: "quit", text: "Quit", action: () => {} }]);
    await system.tray.setTooltip("My app");
    await system.tray.setIcon("icons/tray.png");
    await system.tray.destroy();

    // notify — explicit permission flow; show() never auto-prompts
    const granted = await system.notify.isPermissionGranted();  // SystemResult<boolean>
    await system.notify.requestPermission();                    // SystemResult<boolean>
    await system.notify.show({ title: "Done", body: "..." });   // err("denied") if not granted

    // clipboard — text only
    const text = await system.clipboard.readText();       // SystemResult<string>
    await system.clipboard.writeText("hello");

    // deepLink — launch URL + runtime deliveries (deduped)
    const url = await system.deepLink.getCurrent();       // SystemResult<string | null>
    const unsub = system.deepLink.onOpen(({ url }) => route(url));  // sync, always succeeds
    unsub();

### Narrowing the result

    const r = await system.store.get<number>("count");
    if (r.ok) {
      use(r.value ?? 0);                        // r.value: number | undefined
    } else if (r.reason === "unsupported") {
      hideFeature();                            // permanent absence
    } else {
      console.warn(r.provider, r.reason, r.message);
    }

### Forcing the runtime (tests)

    createApp({
      plugins: [storePlugin],
      pluginConfigs: {
        store: { name: "test-db" },
        runtime: { forceKind: "web", forcePlatform: "macos" }
      }
    });

### Extending (consumer plugin)

    import { createApp, createPlugin } from "@moku-labs/system";
    const myPlugin = createPlugin("my", {
      api: ctx => ({ ping: () => ctx.runtime.kind })  // ctx.runtime, ctx.log, ctx.env available
    });
    const app = createApp({ plugins: [myPlugin] });

## Plugin catalog

One line each: purpose | tier | API | events.

- runtime   — shell/platform detection injected as ctx.runtime; the single override
              point for the seam | Core (Micro, auto-registered) |
              ctx.runtime.kind, ctx.runtime.platform; config { forceKind, forcePlatform }
              (both default null = auto-detect) | no events
- store     — JSON-safe key-value persistence; Tauri store file with awaited save(),
              web IndexedDB via idb-keyval with one-time write-probe | Complex |
              get/set/delete/keys/clear; config { name } default "moku-system" | no events
- tray      — desktop tray icon + menu, created lazily on first mutating call; web and
              Tauri-mobile are all-unsupported | Complex |
              setMenu/setTooltip/setIcon/destroy; config { id } default "moku-system" | no events
- notify    — OS/browser notifications, explicit permission flow (show never
              auto-prompts) | Complex | show/requestPermission/isPermissionGranted;
              NO config | no events
- clipboard — text clipboard; feature-probed, NotAllowedError -> "denied" | Complex |
              readText/writeText; NO config | no events
- deepLink  — deep-link URL delivery, the only push-driven capability; dedups upstream
              getCurrent() replay | Complex | getCurrent/onOpen(cb): Unsubscribe;
              config { schemes } default [] (empty = accept all, lowercase scheme
              pattern validated at onInit) | event "deepLink:open" { url: string }

Naming: plugin name string "deepLink", directory src/plugins/deep-link/, subpath
"@moku-labs/system/deep-link", event "deepLink:open".

## File structure

    src/index.ts                 root entry: createApp, createPlugin, ok, err + types only
    src/config.ts                createCoreConfig("system", ...) — registers logPlugin,
                                 envPlugin, runtimePlugin as core plugins
    src/store.ts                 subpath entry @moku-labs/system/store
    src/tray.ts                  subpath entry @moku-labs/system/tray
    src/notify.ts                subpath entry @moku-labs/system/notify
    src/clipboard.ts             subpath entry @moku-labs/system/clipboard
    src/deep-link.ts             subpath entry @moku-labs/system/deep-link
    src/plugins/runtime/         core plugin + shared seam modules:
      result.ts                  SystemResult contract + ok/err helpers (public)
      provider.ts                resolution lifecycle (internal, not exported)
      detect.ts                  sync, import-free shell/platform detection
    src/plugins/<name>/          each capability: index.ts (createPlugin spec),
      api.ts, state.ts, types.ts, providers/{index,web,tauri,types}.ts,
      __tests__/{unit,integration}/
    tests/                       framework-level tests only (never plugin-specific)

## Conventions

- Package manager: bun exclusively. Scripts: build, test, test:unit, test:integration,
  test:coverage (90% threshold), lint, lint:fix, format, validate.
- Family rules (MC1-MC3): branded CLI kit for any CLI surface; ctx.log (never raw
  console.*); ctx.env (never raw process.env).
- Provider interface types are structural and local — @tauri-apps/* types are never
  re-exported (d.mts leakage guard).
- notify and clipboard take no config; they are excluded from pluginConfigs.
- deepLink onOpen subscription is local and synchronous (always succeeds); on web no
  push deliveries occur in v1. Windows/Linux runtime delivery requires single-instance
  forwarding wired by the native packager repo.
